diffs.diff: output voltage (V): datasheet reading gives 1 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: The MAX4466 is a plain op-amp microphone preamp with an analog voltage output, so the only 'conversion' is identity (1 V per V, offset 0), which is what the second reading reports. The model already encodes exactly that: sim.wave.voltsPerUnit = 1 with centerV 1.65 (VCC/2 bias), and the driver returns OUT in volts (read_uv()/1e6, or read_u16()*3.3/65535). The comparator reports 'none' only because it does not read sim.wave.voltsPerUnit (it reads measure/responses or vAtMin!=vAtMax, and here vAtMin=vAtMax=1.65 since the DC level does not change with loudness). Datasheet: 'converts it to a voltage appearing at the output'; 'The MAX4465-MAX4469 can drive a 10kOhm load and still typically swing within 16mV of the supply rails' (Rail-to-Rail Output Stage, p.7); Supply Voltage Range 2.4 to 5.5 V. No change needed.
